problem: Learned object-goal navigation agents generalize poorly to unfamiliar environments, and classical map-based navigation copes badly with dynamic scenes. The literature on scene graph-based object goal navigation is also scattered and lacks a unified formal description.
motivation: Agents need spatial intelligence, i.e. turning visual observations into insights, understanding and actions, to generalize in unseen environments. Scene graphs give a structured representation of objects and relations that may provide this. The survey aims to show their importance for navigation.
key_idea: Survey scene graph-based object goal navigation by giving a formal description and computational framework, then categorizing methods for constructing and applying scene graphs.
insight: Only the abstract was available, so no ablation detail can be cited. The abstract claims the survey presents experimental evidence that scene graphs improve navigation success, but the details are not visible.
method: Formal description: defines scene graph-based object goal navigation formally and gives a computational framework

results: The abstract states the survey gives experimental evidence that scene graphs improve navigation success, but it reports no specific numbers or baselines.
